definitions.type: Lebesgue measure on the Borel real line, evaluated as an outer measure on arbitrary sets
definitions.definition: λ is the usual Lebesgue measure MeasureTheory.volume on ℝ. For any nonnegative extended-real function f, ∫f dλ denotes its nonnegative Lebesgue integral (the supremum of the integrals of nonnegative measurable simple functions bounded above by f). For a set B and constant c≥0, c 1_B is c on B and zero outside B. For a bounded open interval J=(a,b) with a<b its length |J| means b−a.

inputs.statement: For every nonempty subset B of ℝ which is bounded above, there is a real number b which is a least upper bound of B: every element of B is≤b, and b is≤every upper bound of B.
For every nonempty subset B of ℝ which is bounded below, there is a real number b which is a greatest lower bound of B: b is≤every element of B, and every lower bound of B is≤b.

output.statement: For every nonempty B⊆ℝ, every finite ρ≥0 with |b−b'|≤ρ for all b,b'∈B, and every η>0, B is contained in the bounded open interval J=(inf B−η/2,sup B+η/2), whose length |J| is≤ρ+η. The endpoints exist as real numbers, and the construction also applies when ρ=0.

locals.declaration: Fix an arbitrary subset B of ℝ.
Fix an arbitrary finite real ρ.
For the boundedness argument take any b0∈B; the assumed nonemptiness supplies such a point.
Define J=(inf B−η/2,sup B+η/2), after F001 has established finite endpoints.
In the pairwise comparison let b be any element of B.
In the bound comparison let b' be any element of B.

argument.text: Fix B,ρ,η and assume L1: B is nonempty, ρ≥0, every pair in B has distance≤ρ, and η>0. For any b0∈B the pairwise bound puts B⊆[b0−ρ,b0+ρ]; since B is nonempty, such a center exists and proves both boundedness conditions. M016 and M017 therefore give a real least upper bound and a real greatest lower bound of B. Each is unique by order antisymmetry; denote them sup B and inf B. For every b'∈B, all b∈B satisfy b≤b'+ρ; the least-upper-bound property gives sup B≤b'+ρ. Thus sup B−ρ is a lower bound for B, so the greatest-lower-bound property gives sup B−ρ≤inf B. Therefore sup B−inf B≤ρ, including ρ=0.

produces.statement: B has finite real endpoints inf B and sup B, and sup B−inf B≤ρ.

argument.text: Define J=(inf B−η/2,sup B+η/2) using the endpoints established in F001. Every element of B lies between inf B and sup B, and η>0 makes both endpoint containments strict. The interval is nonempty, open and bounded. Its length is sup B−inf B+η≤ρ+η by F001. Discharge L1 and quantify B,ρ,η to obtain precisely the exported conclusion. This argument asserts no measurability of B.
